questions.question: Maps showing natural feature of the earth such as mountains, plateaus, rivers, plains, oceans, etc. are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Relief Map__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A raised-relief map** or **terrain model** is a three-dimensional representation, **usually of terrain**, materialized as a **physical artefact.**
 
• When representing terrain, **the vertical dimension** is usually **exaggerated by a factor between five and ten.**
 
• This facilitates the **visual recognition** of **terrain features.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Political Map** - A Political Map represents countries, states, and towns. Often they are painted in different colours so we can see them better. This map shows names and boundaries.
 
• **Topographic Map** - Topography concerns the shape and character of the Earth's surface, and maps were among the first artefacts to record these observations.
 
• **Thematic Map** - A thematic map is a type of map that portrays the geographic pattern of a particular subject matter (theme) in a geographic area like temperature, language, or population.

Source:

https://ncert.nic.in/ncerts/l/fess204.pdf

questions.question:
Which of the following pair regarding peninsular plateau of India is correct?

I. Central Highlands – south of Narmada river

II. Deccan Plateau – north of Narmada river
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Central Highlands: **The **Central Highlands **are located **north of the Narmada River. **

 
 
• They cover parts of **Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra.**
 
• This region consists of a series of **plateaus, hills, and valleys.**
 
• It is characterized by its average elevation of about **600-900 meters** above **sea level,** making it relatively higher in comparison to the surrounding plains.
 
• The** Central Highlands** are known for their rugged terrain, with prominent hill ranges such as the Vindhya Range and the Satpura Range. These ranges act as a natural boundary between northern and southern India.
 
 
 
• **Deccan Plateau: **The **Deccan Plateau **is situated **south of the Narmada River **and covers a significant portion of **peninsular India**.
 
 
• It spans across several states, including **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.**
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** is a vast elevated region with an average height of about** 600-900 meters** above sea level, although there are certain areas where it reaches higher elevations.
 
• It is characterized by its gently rolling terrain, with extensive lava flows and volcanic activity in the past.
 
• The plateau is composed of layers of basaltic lava flows, giving rise to **black soil, **which is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Peninsular Plateau**, also known as the **Deccan Plateau**, is a large **plateau region in India**.
 
• It is located in the southern part of the Indian subcontinent and covers a major portion of the country.

questions.question: The rivers Damodar, Brahmani and Kharkai originate from the state of _______ in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Jharkhand.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rivers Damodar, Brahmani, and Kharkai originate from the state of **Jharkhand **in India.
 
• Jharkhand fares poorly in terms of canal irrigation because the area is hilly.
 
• Most of the rivers of Jharkhand are seasonal in nature.
 
• They remain dry throughout the year but during the monsoon, season water gets overflowed in these rivers.
 
• As the monsoon approaches the whole country the water level in other higher rivers also increases which flows down to the rivers of Jharkhand thus causing floods in different districts of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• North-East Jharkhand areas like Sahibganj, Godda are very much prone to floods because the Ganga River passes through the surrounding areas.
 
• **Much of Jharkhand lies on the Chota Nagpur Plateau where many rivers pass through such as Damodar, Brahmani, Koel, Subarnarekha, and Kharkai rivers.**
 
• The main concentration of canal irrigation is in the northern plain of India. The digging of canals in rocky and uneven areas is difficult and uneconomic.
 
• The undulating relief and hard rocks make it difficult to dig canals and wells.
 
• It is also difficult to artificially flow water from ground level to the level of hills. It is not economical to use this much electrical energy to lift water.

questions.question: How many countries share the natural heritage of the Caspian Sea?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caspian Sea **

 
 
• The **Caspian Sea**, which is frequently referred to as the** largest lake **or **a true sea,** is the** largest inland body of water in the entire planet**.
 
• An **endorheic basin**, it is located between **Europe and Asia**, which is bordered by the **Caucasus Mountains** to the east,** the Iranian Plateau** to the north, the rich plains of **Southern Russia **to the south, and the wide** steppe of Central Asia to the west**.
 
• With the exception of the extremely salty lagoon of **Garabogazköl **to the east, it has a surface area of 1**43,550 sq mi (372,000 km²)** and a** volume of 78,200 km³**.
 
• The natural heritage of Caspian sea are shared **by five countries** including, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Turkmenistan.
 
• **Kazakhstan **to the northeast**, Russia** to the northwest,** Azerbaijan **to the southwest,** Iran **to the south, and** Turkmenistan **to the southeast form the borders of the Caspian Sea.
 
• The Caspian Sea is famous for its** caviar and oil industries and is home to a variety of species**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://ifpnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/89857-004-0D011EC4.gif] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Like the Black Sea, the **Caspian Sea** is a remnant of the former** Paratethys Sea**.
 
• **Other names of Caspian Sea**
 
 
• The lake is known as the **Mazandaran Sea in Iran**, named for the **famous Mazandaran Province** that sits on its southern banks.
 
• In early **Russian sources** it is mentioned as **The Khvalyn or Khvalis Sea** (after the name of Khwarezmia).
 
• In classical antiquity, it was the **Hyrcanian ocean among the Greeks and Persians**.
 
• The **Abbacuch Sea, Mar de Bachu,** or **Mar de Sala** were the names given to it on **maps made in the Renaissance Europe**.
 
 
 
• In order to further c**onserve the Caspian Sea's biodiversity, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev** signed the Protocol for the Protection of the **Caspian Sea against Pollution from Land-based Sources on October 23, 2021**.

questions.question: What is the name of the oceanic trench in the Indian Ocean with a maximum depth of 23,560 feet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Java Trench**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Java Trench:-**

 
 
• **The oceanic trench in the Indian Ocean with a maximum depth of 23,560 feet is the Java Trench.**
 
• It is located south of the Indonesian island of Java, and is the deepest point in the Indian Ocean.
 
• **The Java Trench is a subduction zone, where the Indo-Australian Plate is sliding underneath the Eurasian Plate.**
 
• This process creates intense heat and pressure, which can lead to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tonga Trench:-**

 
 
• **It is the deepest oceanic trench in the Southern Hemisphere, with a maximum depth of 35,853 feet (10,932 meters). **
 
• It is located in the South Pacific Ocean, east of the Tonga archipelago.
 
• The Tonga Trench is a subduction zone, where the Pacific Plate is sliding underneath the Indo-Australian Plate.
 
 
 
• **Amirante Trench:-**
 
 
• **It is the deepest oceanic trench in the Indian Ocean, with a maximum depth of 21,959 feet (6,695 meters). **
 
• It is located in the western Indian Ocean, south of the Amirante Islands.
 
• The Amirante Trench is a transform fault, where two tectonic plates are sliding past each other. This process creates intense friction, which can lead to earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Diamantina Trench:-**
 
 
• **It is a fracture zone in the Indian Ocean, extending westward from the southwest coast of Australia. **
 
• It is not a true oceanic trench, as it does not have the same depth or structure as other trenches such as the Tonga Trench or the Amirante Trench.

questions.question: Which plateau, with an average elevation of about 600 meters (2000 feet), is bounded by three mountain ranges: the Satpura range to the north and the Eastern and Western Ghats on either side?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The large **Deccan Plateau **in **southern India **is located **between **the **Western Ghats **and the **Eastern Ghats**.
 
• It is **loosely defined **as the **peninsular region **between **these ranges **that is **south **of the **Narmada river**. 
 
• To **the north**, it is **bounded by **the **Satpura **and **Vindhya Ranges**.
 
• **The plateau **is **drier than **the **coastal region **of **India**.
 
• **It ranges between 100 and 1,000 meters **(330 and 3,280 ft), with an average **elevation **of about **600 meters (2,000 ft).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marwar **(also called the Jodhpur region) is a region of **southwestern Rajasthan **state in **North Western India**. It lies **partly **in the **Thar Desert**.
 
• **The Meghalaya plateau **is traditionally **divided **into **Garo**, **Khasi **and **Jaintia Hills**. The region from the river **Dhansiri **in the east to the **Singimari River. **
 
• The **Chota Nagpur Plateau **is a plateau in **eastern India**, which **covers **much of **Jharkhand state **as well as **adjacent parts of Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh**.

questions.question: Which is the largest river island in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Majuli island.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The **Guinness Book of World Records** has named Majuli as the world's largest river island.
 
• The beautiful river island is located on the **River Brahmaputra** in **Assam**.
 
• It is formed by the Brahmaputra River in the South, and **Kherkutia Xuti,** an anabranch of Brahmaputra, joined by the Subansiri River in the north.
 
• The island is populated by the **Mising, Deori, and Sonowal Kachri **tribes. 
 
• The people of the island speak the languages of **Mising, Assamese, and Deori.**
 
• It is home to about **1,60,000** individuals and is a hub of neo-Vaishnavite Assamese culture. 
 
• It covers about **880 sq km** of land and is one of Assam's popular tourist destinations.
 
• Majuli suffers from heavy erosion due to the regular flooding of the Brahmaputra river.
 
• It is estimated that it has lost approximately one-third of its territory in the last 30-40 years due to erosion. 
 
• It was recently declared a district and was previously a subdivision under the district of J**orhat.** 
 
• It has also been included in the tentative list of **UNESCO's World Heritage Sites**.

questions.question: India shares its land boundaries with which countries in the east?
questions.solution:

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

questions.question: The Arctic Ocean is located within the Arctic Circle and surrounds the North Pole. It is connected with the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as ______ strait.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Bering'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bering Strait:**

 
 
• The Bering Strait is a narrow passage of water between Russia and Alaska.
 
• It connects the Arctic Ocean (via the Chukchi Sea) with the Pacific Ocean (via the Bering Sea).
 
• The strait is about 85 km wide at its narrowest point and is relatively shallow, with a depth of around 50 meters.
 
• It has been historically significant for human migration, as it is believed early humans crossed a land bridge here during the Ice Age.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e94a93e26336f4c54da9e84abf46923cbefc092d9ad39fa0ba1f9ed28ceb440.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palk Strait:**

 
 
• This strait lies between India and Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal and the Gulf of Mannar.
 
• It has no geographical relation to the Arctic Ocean.
 
 
 
• **Hudson Strait:**
 
 
• Located in northeastern Canada, it connects Hudson Bay with the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• Though in the northern latitudes, it does not connect the Arctic and Pacific Oceans.
 
 
 
• **Bosphorus Strait:**
 
 
• This important waterway in Turkey connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara, and ultimately the Mediterranean Sea.
 
• It is far from the Arctic region and plays no role in linking the Arctic Ocean with the Pacific.
